dimensions.reasons: The author final image `.eval_workspace/exports/temple_courtyard.png` clearly shows an open walled courtyard, a centered red-columned main hall, gold roof, straight central approach, guardian-statue pair, trees, and warm evening-like illumination. However, several specifically requested focal details do not read as intended.
issues: The guardian figures look like rounded cartoon animal/bear-or-squirrel statues rather than identifiable traditional stone lions.
The central bronze object reads as a small incense burner with upright sticks, not a large bell.
The lanterns are predominantly cream-white with red tassels and are strung below the hall eaves, rather than reading as hanging red lanterns grouped in a corner.
The architecture is a simplified pavilion interpretation with minimal traditional ornament and no readable plaque text.

issues: Some guardian-pedestal accessories appear as arbitrary loose blocks and spheres rather than integrated architectural details.
The very broad roof slabs and projecting eaves are structurally stylized and somewhat heavy relative to the visible supporting framework.

issues: The supposed lions have toy-like rounded silhouettes, visible bead eyes and snouts, and do not independently read as stone lion guardians.

Lantern bodies are pale cream rather than red.

issues: The plastic-gloss red columns, uniformly smooth guardian figures, geometric conifer trees, and slab-like roof create a toy-diorama appearance rather than a believable old-town temple.
Warm bloom, soft haze, and noise on the gold roof reduce crispness and material credibility.
The scene lacks the weathering, carved detail, tiled roof structure, and ornamental richness expected of a quaint historic courtyard promo.

issues: The author final image is effectively a centered frontal view rather than a camera at the gateway angled into the courtyard.

dimensions.reasons: The essential hall, courtyard enclosure, straight approach, surrounding foliage, hanging lantern forms, and two flanking guardian statues are present in the final export.
issues: A pair of recognizable stone lions is not present; the figures remain generic cartoon animals.

criteria.criterion: The delivered final image is a finished, characterful, quaint, and elegant promotional depiction of a traditional Chinese temple courtyard.
criteria.evidence: The authored final image temple_courtyard.png is a complete, composed promotional-style render: a symmetrical open courtyard frames a red-columned hall, formal central approach, paving, perimeter walls, lanterns, trees, and decorative entry figures. The warm gold/red architectural palette and layered roof treatment clearly communicate a stylized traditional temple setting.

criteria.criterion: The principal main hall combines visual dominance, red columns, and a golden traditional upturned-eave roof.
criteria.evidence: temple_courtyard.png clearly centers the hall as the largest and dominant structure. Numerous glossy red cylindrical columns support a broad gold roof with layered fascia and visibly rising/slanted corner-eave elements in a traditional Chinese-inspired form.

criteria.criterion: Two recognizable carved-stone guardian lions form a paired installation at the gateway.
criteria.evidence: The two paired entry statues in temple_courtyard.png have rounded soft-bodied animal forms with bead eyes, snouts, ears, and curled tails; they read as stylized bear/squirrel-like figures rather than recognizable Chinese guardian lions. Their smooth pale surfaces also do not visibly read as carved stone.

criteria.criterion: The open courtyard, straight bluestone route to the hall, and relative orientation of all major elements form a clearly readable layout.
criteria.evidence: The final frontal render shows an open, readable court with a long straight cool gray-blue paved strip running directly to the hall steps. The paired entry statues flank the near approach, while the hall, steps, side structures, and open cobbled areas remain spatially legible.

criteria.criterion: A defined courtyard corner contains the complete large bronze-bell and plausibly suspended red-lantern vignette.
criteria.evidence: No large recognizable bronze temple bell is visible in a courtyard corner. The small reflective brass object at the hall steps has upright rods and reads more like an incense burner or bowl, while the visible suspended lanterns are cream/gold rather than red and are not presented with a bell as a corner vignette.

criteria.criterion: The final image combines a recognizable warm dusk atmosphere with bright, readable courtyard detail.
criteria.evidence: temple_courtyard.png uses warm amber illumination, a pinkish twilight-like sky, long soft structural shadows, and lit hanging lanterns while retaining clear visibility of the hall, approach path, statues, and courtyard paving.

criteria.criterion: The usable native project contains the complete authored scene and implements the requested inward-angled gateway camera view.

notes: The submission clearly establishes a warm, open, centered temple courtyard with a readable red-and-gold main hall and strong path-to-hall organization. It falls well short on key requested identity objects: the guardian statues are not convincingly lions, the bell does not read as a bell, and the red corner lantern feature is absent. The final is also more toy-like and frontal than a quaint, elegant angled gateway promo image.
